artifacts.summary: Root-causes and verifies fixes for all five agent-system defects (batch gate deferral paths, Goals-header anchor, plan-compliance polarity inversion, literature --read path resolution, gate16 routing_agents_hard), with two factual corrections to the dispatch's own evidence (Defect 2 is a loud exit 71, not a vacuous pass; Defect 5's routing_hard key does not exist).

memory_candidates.content: jq's object-constructor syntax (e.g. jq '{key, other}' file.json) renders an ABSENT key as JSON null in its output, visually indistinguishable from a genuinely-declared-null key. Use jq -r 'has("key")' (or a direct language-native key-presence check) to distinguish 'key is absent' from 'key is present with value null' -- never infer presence from a constructed-object null.

In lean-challenge-snapshot.sh (extensions/lean/scripts/), the Goals-block extraction's PREAMBLE rule (any line before the first bulleted line is never scanned for identifiers) already tolerates arbitrary intervening prose, including a multi-line parenthetical before the header's colon -- the only requirement is that the Goals header's FIRST line match the start-of-range regex. When widening a Goals-header anchor regex, dropping a trailing-punctuation requirement (e.g. the colon) is usually sufficient and safe, since downstream bullet-scanning logic is already anchor-position-agnostic.

orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's established fix for a script path that may live at either the deployed .claude/scripts/ location or the agent-system source-store location is a two-candidate existence-checked array (deployed path first, source-store path fallback), e.g. hb_lib_candidates for phase-heartbeat-lib.sh (lines ~264-274). Any new dispatch-text directive naming a script path should resolve it the same way rather than hardcoding one form.
